route: WordPress REST API /wp-json/wp/v2/posts, paginated, date from REST local 'date'
notes: robots.txt (200): 'User-agent: *' + empty 'Disallow:' (only /tag/ and only for Meta-WebIndexer/Meta-ExternalAgent), 'crawl-delay: 10', Sitemap: /sitemap_index.xml. The sitemap tree is DEAD for recent posts: /sitemap_index.xml (200, 493 entries) has no lastmod newer than 2026-06-23 on ANY entry, Yoast's cache has not regenerated since June, so post-sitemap1..214 and news-sitemap.xml stop at 2026-06-23 - this is why the earlier attempt reported 'sitemap parsing lacked dates'. That route is closed, not just awkward. Live route: the site's own WordPress REST API, GET /wp-json/wp/v2/posts?per_page=100&orderby=date&order=desc&_fields=date,date_gmt,link&after=..&before=..&page=N (200, current to the minute: first page was 2026-10-27T07:33 local). One gotcha cost one run: passing an explicit offset 'after=2026-09-24T00:00:00+01:00' returns an EMPTY list, because the unencoded '+' in a query string decodes to a space and WP rejects the date; the fix is percent-encoding and naive local times (site tz Africa/Lagos +01:00, no DST). Window is queried with a 2-day margin on both sides and filtered locally by the date part of the response, so no boundary post is lost or misdated. Pagination stops when a page's oldest date is before 2026-09-25 (19 pages x 100 = 1792 rows for 31 days, ~50-90 posts/day); retries with backoff on 429/5xx, and a per-day re-query safety net if any target day came back under 15 rows (not needed). Listed date = date part of the REST field 'date', the site's own local publication time; 'modified' is edit time and is ignored. Verified by re-fetching 4 articles (2026-09-30, 10-05, 10-10, 10-20): all 200, 10,767-12,957 characters of text, and each page's JSON-LD datePublished (+ article:published_time) equals the listed date exactly (e.g. 2026-09-30T10:28:04+00:00). Output: data/urls_custom/premiumtimesng-com.tsv, 1792 rows, 0 duplicates, 0 dates outside the window, minimum 24 on 2026-09-26, all 31 days covered. Runtime ~4 min, dominated by the site's crawl-delay: 10. Note for others: a WP site's robots.txt Disallow list being empty does not mean its Yoast sitemap is alive - check the newest lastmod in the index before trusting per-day or per-month sitemap files, and remember that a literal '+' in a REST after/before value silently returns zero results instead of an error.
